1.explanation: This code renders a Carbon DataTable with a TableToolbar that contains three icon actions plus a primary button. By wrapping the table in a narrow container (360px wide), the toolbar’s responsive behavior collapses the last actions into an OverflowMenu toggle. That toggle renders as a “•••” icon button whose default aria-label is “Menu” (and no visible text), causing an accessible-name mismatch (IBM 2.5.3 Label in Name). You can reproduce the violation by running this code and inspecting the overflow button with an accessibility scanner.
1.bug_scenario: In our Storybook, when you render a DataTable with a toolbar containing several actions (e.g. Download, Edit, Settings, plus a primary button) inside a narrow container, Carbon’s responsive toolbar will collapse the extra actions into an OverflowMenu. That OverflowMenu toggle renders a button with aria-label="Menu" and a “•••” icon, but no visible text, so its accessible name (‘Menu’) does not match any visible label. DAP flags this as an IBM 2.5.3 “Label in Name” violation.
